entries.name: Ren 仁
entries.note: a Wei town near Pingqiu.

entries.name: Pingqiu 平丘
entries.note: modern Fengqiu, Henan.

entries.name: Huang 黄
entries.note: the old Huang city east of Kaocheng County (Zhengyi); modern Minquan, Henan.

entries.name: Jiyang 济阳
entries.note: the old Jiyang city south-west of Wanju County (Zhengyi); modern Lankao, Henan.

entries.name: Puli 濮磿
entries.note: a place near the Pu River (Suoyin), which flows north into the Ji at Juye (Xu Guang); around modern Puyang, Henan.

entries.name: Yuci 榆次
entries.note: a city of Zhao in the Taiyuan region, south-east of Jinyang; modern Yuci, Jinzhong, Shanxi.
entries.more: where Zhi Bo was defeated (Suoyin); modern Yuci, Jinzhong, Shanxi.

entries.name: Wu 吴
entries.note: the state of Wu and its capital; modern Suzhou, Jiangsu.

pages.label: 249 BC · Appendix: text of the Zhanguo Zonghengjia Shu
247 BC · Ivar the Boneless' commentary and analysis I

entries.name: Gansui 干隧
entries.note: in the Wu country, forty li north-west of Suzhou, where King Fuchai of Wu killed himself (Zhengyi).

entries.name: Yue 越
entries.note: the state of Yue, with its capital at Kuaiji; modern Shaoxing, Zhejiang.

pages.label: 249 BC · Appendix: text of the Zhanguo Zonghengjia Shu
247 BC · Ivar the Boneless' commentary and analysis I

entries.name: Ailing 艾陵
entries.note: Ai Mountain, sixty li south of Bo County in Yanzhou (Zhengyi); modern Tai'an, Shandong.

entries.name: shore of Sanzhu 三渚之浦
entries.note: in the Wu country near Gusu; the Zhanguoce has 三江之浦, the shore of the Three Rivers.

entries.name: Jinyang 晋阳
entries.note: the Zhao stronghold; modern Taiyuan, Shanxi.

pages.label: 247 BC · Ivar the Boneless' commentary and analysis II

entries.name: Zao Terrace 凿台
entries.note: a terrace at Yuci (Xu Guang), by the Dongguo River (Zhengyi).

entries.name: Sui River 随水
entries.note: the river at Sui; modern Suizhou, Hubei.

entries.name: Liu 留
entries.note: modern Pei County, Jiangsu.

entries.name: Fangyu 方与
entries.note: modern Yutai, Shandong.

entries.name: Zhi 铚
entries.note: modern Suzhou (宿州), Anhui.

entries.name: Huling 湖陵
entries.note: south-east of modern Yutai, Shandong.

entries.name: Dang 砀
entries.note: modern Dangshan, Anhui.

entries.name: Xiao 萧
entries.note: modern Xiao County, Anhui.

entries.name: Xiang 相
entries.note: modern Suixi, Anhui.

entries.name: the Si country 泗上
entries.note: the lands along the Si River, between Lu and Chu.

entries.name: the River 河
entries.note: the Yellow River.

entries.name: the eastern mountains 东山
entries.note: the mountains east of Qin's passes, the Xiao range.

entries.name: Zheng 郑
entries.note: the capital of Han; modern Xinzheng, Henan.

entries.name: Xu 许
entries.note: modern Xuchang, Henan.

entries.name: Yanling 鄢陵
entries.note: modern Yanling, Henan.

entries.name: Shangcai 上蔡
entries.note: modern Shangcai, Henan.

entries.name: Shaoling 召陵
entries.note: modern Luohe, Henan.

entries.name: the land north of the Huai 淮北
entries.note: Chu's lands north of the Huai River; northern Anhui and Jiangsu.

entries.name: Jiangdong 江东
entries.note: the lands east of the lower Yangzi; southern Jiangsu.

entries.name: Lanling 兰陵
entries.note: modern Lanling County, Shandong.

entries.name: the upper lands 上地
entries.note: Han's highland territory towards Shangdang, in south-eastern Shanxi.

pages.label: 255 BC · Ivar the Boneless' commentary and analysis II

entries.name: Wucheng 吴城
entries.note: a Wei town in Dayang (Xu Guang); the old city of Yu on Yu Mountain, also called Wu Mountain, fifty li north-east of Hebei County in Shanzhou (Zhengyi, citing the Kuodi zhi); modern Pinglu County, Shanxi.

entries.name: Shuzhou 徐州
entries.note: east of Lu, the Xue County of Han times (Xu Guang); the Shuowen writes it 䣄, and the Suoyin gives its pronunciation as that of 舒, shu; modern Tengzhou, Shandong.

entries.name: Yong 雍
entries.note: the old capital of Qin and seat of its altars; modern Fengxiang, Baoji, Shaanxi.

entries.name: Juyang 鉅陽
entries.note: Chu's seat after Chen; identified with the Diandingzi walled site at Juyang village, Gongji, in Taihe County, Anhui, on the Xifei River.

entries.name: Songzi 宋子
entries.note: a Zhao town; Xu Guang: in Julu; north-east of modern Zhao County, Hebei.

entries.name: Weiwen 尉文
entries.note: the fief granted to Lian Po; the Suoyin: probably a place name, or else 尉 an office and 文 a name; the Zhengyi: probably land in Weizhou (modern Yu County, Hebei).

entries.name: Dongwucheng 东武城
entries.note: Lord Pingyuan's fief; Xu Guang: in Qinghe; the Zhengyi: Wucheng County in Beizhou; modern Wucheng, Shandong.

entries.name: Yiling 夷陵
entries.note: the burial ground of the kings of Chu; modern Yichang, Hubei.

entries.name: Li 李
entries.note: the fief of Li Tong's father; Xu Guang: Li city in Chenggao in Henei; the Zhengyi: Wen County in Huaizhou was originally Li city; modern Wen County, Henan.

entries.name: Fanyang 繁阳
entries.note: a Wei town; Xu Guang: in Wei Commandery; the Zhengyi: north-east of Neihuang County in Xiangzhou; modern Neihuang, Henan.

entries.name: Eastern Zhou 东周
entries.note: the Eastern Zhou domain, the eastern of the two fiefs into which the Zhou royal house was divided, centred on Gong (modern Gongyi, Henan).

entries.name: Chenggao 成皋
entries.note: a Han town; the Zhengyi: the old Eastern Guo, Zheng's town of Zhi, also called Hulao, the Han dynasty's Chenggao; north-west of modern Xingyang, Henan.

entries.name: Gong 巩
entries.note: a Han town; the Zhengyi: Gong County in Luozhou; modern Gongyi, Henan.

entries.name: Yangren 阳人
entries.note: Xu Guang: the Yangren settlement in Liang County of Henan; the Zhengyi: the old Yangren city forty li west of Liang County in Ruzhou; west of modern Ruzhou, Henan.

entries.name: Sanchuan Commandery 三川郡
entries.note: a Qin Commandery, named for its three rivers, the Yellow River, Luo River and Yi River (Wei Zhao); established in 249 BC on the lands of Zhou and Han around Luoyang; renamed Henan Commandery under the Han (Pei Yin).

entries.name: Xingyang 荥阳
entries.note: a Han town east of Chenggao; modern Xingyang, Henan.

entries.name: Bian 卞
entries.note: a Lu town; east of modern Sishui, Shandong.

entries.name: Ke 柯
entries.note: a Qi settlement; the Suoyin cites Du Yu, now Dong'e in Jibei; the old Dong'e city, south-east of modern Yanggu, Shandong.

entries.name: Henan 河南
entries.note: the Han name of Sanchuan Commandery, the lands around Luoyang; the Shiji uses it of Qin's commandery (Suoyin).

entries.name: Luoyang 雒阳
entries.note: the old Zhou capital on the Luo; modern Luoyang, Henan.

entries.name: Langya 琅琊
entries.note: the seat of the kings of Yue after Goujian; placed by tradition at the Langya of Shandong (modern Jiaonan, Qingdao), and by the report cited here at Jinpingshan, Lianyungang, Jiangsu. Written 瑯琊 and 琅邪 as well.

entries.name: Jiang 江
entries.note: the Yangzi.

entries.name: Huai 淮
entries.note: the Huai River.

entries.name: Jin 晋
entries.note: the state of Jin, in modern Shanxi, from which Han, Zhao and Wei were formed.

entries.name: Wu Commandery 吴郡
entries.note: the Han Commandery of Wu, around modern Suzhou, Jiangsu.

entries.name: An County 安县
entries.note: a County of Wu Commandery under the Han, listed in the Xu Hanshu's Treatise on Commanderies and Kingdoms; north of modern Jiaxing, Zhejiang.

entries.name: Xicen tomb 西岑冢
entries.note: a tomb in Wu Commandery named in the Yuejue.

entries.name: Jinpingshan 锦屏山
entries.note: a hill at Lianyungang, Jiangsu, formerly Qushan and Langyashan, with the walled site at Jiulongkou.

entries.name: Qushan 朐山
entries.note: the earlier name of Jinpingshan at Lianyungang, Jiangsu.

entries.name: Qu County 朐县
entries.note: the Qin County at Qushan; modern Lianyungang, Jiangsu.

entries.name: Langya Terrace 琅琊台
entries.note: the terrace raised by the First Emperor of Qin on the coast of Langya; modern Jiaonan, Qingdao, Shandong.

entries.name: Fengtian 奉天
entries.note: Fengtian in pinyin, Hōten in Japanese reading; the Mukden of the Western press of the day. The seat of the Fengtian clique; modern Shenyang, Liaoning.

entries.name: Shimenzi 石門子
entries.note: Shimenzi in pinyin, Sekimonshi in Japanese reading: the Shimenzhai 石門寨 of the Chinese accounts, in the hills north-west of Shanhai Pass; modern Shimenzhai, Qinhuangdao, Hebei.

entries.name: Jinzhou 錦州
entries.note: Jinzhou in pinyin, Kinshū in Japanese reading; a city of western Fengtian province; modern Jinzhou, Liaoning.

entries.name: Qingdao 青島
entries.note: Qingdao in pinyin, Chintao in Japanese reading; the port on the Shandong coast; modern Qingdao.

entries.name: Qinhuangdao 秦皇島
entries.note: Qinhuangdao in pinyin, Shinkōtō in Japanese reading; the port on the Bohai coast west of Shanhai Pass; modern Qinhuangdao, Hebei.

entries.name: Shanhai Pass 山海關
entries.note: Shanhaiguan in pinyin, Sankaikan in Japanese reading; the Pass where the Great Wall meets the sea, on the road from Hebei into Manchuria; modern Shanhaiguan, Qinhuangdao, Hebei.

entries.name: Tianjin 天津
entries.note: Tianjin in pinyin, Tenshin in Japanese reading; the port city on the Hai River; modern Tianjin.

entries.name: Beijing 北京
entries.note: Beijing in pinyin, Pekin in Japanese reading; the capital of the Republic in 1924; modern Beijing.

entries.name: Ju 沮
entries.note: a County of Qin in Hanzhong Commandery, on the upper Ju River 沮水 (the Jialing); modern Lueyang 略阳, Shaanxi.

pages.label: 249 BC · Qin slips in the Yuelu Academy collection

entries.name: Nanzheng 南郑
entries.note: a County of Qin, the seat of Hanzhong Commandery, in the Han River valley; modern Hanzhong 汉中, Shaanxi.

pages.label: 249 BC · Qin slips in the Yuelu Academy collection

entries.name: Suxu 宿胥
entries.note: a place on the Yellow River in Wei, Suxu Mouth 宿胥口, where the river's old course turned north; modern Xun County 浚县, Henan.

pages.label: 249 BC · Appendix: text of the Zhanguo Zonghengjia Shu

entries.name: Kuaiji 会稽
entries.note: the mountain in Yue on which King Goujian was besieged by Wu in 494 BC; modern Shaoxing, Zhejiang.

pages.label: 249 BC · Appendix: text of the Zhanguo Zonghengjia Shu

entries.name: Yinjin 阴晋
entries.note: a town of Wei on the Qin border east of the Hua mountain, taken by Qin in 332 BC and renamed Ningqin 宁秦; modern Huayin 华阴, Shaanxi.

pages.label: 249 BC · Appendix: text of the Zhanguo Zonghengjia Shu

entries.name: Shangluo 上雒
entries.note: a County of Qin on the upper Luo River, on the road from the Guanzhong to Nanyang; modern Shangluo 商洛, Shaanxi.

pages.label: 249 BC · Appendix: text of the Zhanguo Zonghengjia Shu

entries.name: Taiyuan 太原
entries.note: the basin of the middle Fen River, Zhao's north-western region, made a Commandery of Qin; modern Taiyuan, Shanxi.

entries.name: Xincheng 新城
entries.note: a city of Zhao, also called Xiaopingcheng 小平城; the Zhengyi places it forty-seven li south-west of Shanyang County in Shuozhou; modern Shuozhou 朔州, Shanxi.

entries.name: Langmeng 狼孟
entries.note: a city of Zhao north of Jinyang, later a County of Taiyuan Commandery (Jijie); modern Yangqu 阳曲, Shanxi.

entries.name: Gaodu 高都
entries.note: a city of Wei in the hills south of Shangdang; the Zhengyi: its old city is Zezhou; modern Jincheng 晋城, Shanxi.

entries.name: Ji 汲
entries.note: a city of Wei in Henei, north of the Yellow River; the Zhengyi: its old city twenty-five li south-west of Ji County in Weizhou; modern Weihui 卫辉, Henan.

entries.name: Shangdang 上党
entries.note: the upland region between the Taihang and the Fen, held in parts by Han and Zhao and contested with Qin; modern Changzhi 长治, Shanxi.

entries.name: Longdui 龙兑
entries.note: a town of Zhao on the Yan border; the Zhengyi takes it from the Longshan of the Kuodizhi, twenty-five li south-west of Suicheng County in Yizhou; modern Xushui 徐水, Hebei.

entries.name: Fenmen 汾门
entries.note: a town of Zhao on the Yan border; the Jijie (Xu Guang): in Beixincheng; the Zhengyi suspects 汾 an error for the Longmen gorge of the Xu River, in the lands of Suicheng, Yongle, Gu'an and Xincheng; modern Xushui 徐水, Hebei.

entries.name: Linle 临乐
entries.note: a town of Zhao on the Yan border; the Jijie: Fangcheng has a Linxiang; the Zhengyi: the old city of Linxiang seventeen li south of Gu'an in Youzhou; modern Gu'an 固安, Hebei.

entries.name: Ge 葛
entries.note: a town of Yan; the Jijie: Gecheng in Gaoyang; the Zhengyi: also called Xihe city, fifty li north-west of Gaoyang County in Yingzhou; modern Gaoyang 高阳, Hebei.

entries.name: Wuyang 武阳
entries.note: the lower capital of Yan 燕下都 on the Yi River; modern Yixian 易县, Hebei.

entries.name: Pingshu 平舒
entries.note: a town of Yan; the Jijie: in Dai Commandery; the Zhengyi: its old city ninety-three li north of Lingqiu County in Weizhou; modern Guangling 广灵, Shanxi.

entries.name: Rong 戎
entries.note: the lands of the Rong peoples west of Qin; the Western Rong 西戎 of Duke Mu's hegemony.

entries.name: Wan 宛
entries.note: a city of Chu on the upper Han; modern Nanyang 南阳, Henan.

entries.name: Ba 巴
entries.note: the state and region of Ba on the upper Yangzi, taken by Qin in 316 BC; modern Chongqing.

entries.name: Shu 蜀
entries.note: the state and region of Shu, the Chengdu plain, taken by Qin in 316 BC; the 西蜀 of the memorial.

entries.name: Shang Commandery 上郡
entries.note: the Commandery north of the Wei on the Luo, ceded by Wei to Qin; the Zhengyi: fifteen Counties, in King Huiwen's tenth year; modern northern Shaanxi.

entries.name: Hanzhong 汉中
entries.note: the upper Han valley, taken from Chu by Qin; the Zhengyi: six hundred li, in King Huiwen's thirteenth year; modern Hanzhong, Shaanxi.

entries.name: Jiangnan 江南
entries.note: the lands south of the Yangzi.

entries.name: Taishan 太山
entries.note: Mount Tai 泰山, written 太山; modern Tai'an, Shandong.

entries.name: Kunshan 昆山
entries.note: the jade mountain of the far west; the Zhengyi: Kun'gang, four hundred li north-east of Khotan.

entries.name: Sui 随
entries.note: the state of Sui on the Han, of the pearl of Marquis Sui; modern Suizhou, Hubei.

entries.name: E 阿
entries.note: Dong'e 东阿 of Qi, source of fine silk (Jijie); modern Yanggu, Shandong.

entries.name: Sangjian 桑间
entries.note: a place on the Pu River in Wey, proverbial for its licentious music.

entries.name: Pinglu 平陆
entries.note: a town on Qi's western border (Suoyin), a County of Yanzhou in the names of the Tang (Zhengyi); modern Wenshang, Shandong.

pages.label: 247 BC · Ivar the Boneless' commentary and analysis I

entries.name: Liaocheng 聊城
entries.note: a Qi city on the lower Yellow River; a County of Bozhou in the names of the Tang (Zhengyi); modern Liaocheng, Shandong.

pages.label: 247 BC · Ivar the Boneless' commentary and analysis I

entries.name: Nanyang 南阳 (of Qi)
entries.note: Qi's southern lands, which the Suoyin takes as its lands north of the Huai and on the Si; distinct from Han's Nanyang.

pages.label: 247 BC · Ivar the Boneless' commentary and analysis I

entries.name: Jibei 济北
entries.note: the land north of the Ji River, the region of Liaocheng (Suoyin); modern north-western Shandong.

pages.label: 247 BC · Ivar the Boneless' commentary and analysis I

entries.name: Guan 管
entries.note: a Han town east of Zheng, the old Guan of the Zhou fief; modern Zhengzhou, Henan.

pages.label: 247 BC · Ivar the Boneless' commentary and analysis II

entries.name: Shang 商
entries.note: the Shang state and dynasty, with its late capital at Yin, modern Anyang, Henan.

entries.name: Ordos 鄂尔多斯
entries.note: the Ordos plateau within the great bend of the Yellow River; modern Ordos, Inner Mongolia.

entries.name: northern Shaanxi 陕北
entries.note: the loess highlands of northern Shaanxi, between the Ordos and the Wei valley.

entries.name: Guanzhong 关中
entries.note: the Wei River valley "within the passes", the heartland of Qin; modern central Shaanxi.

entries.name: Beicun, Yao County 耀县北村
entries.note: a Shang-culture site at Beicun in the former Yao County 耀县, since 2002 Yaozhou District 耀州区 of Tongchuan, Shaanxi.

entries.name: Yijiabu, Fufeng 扶风壹家堡
entries.note: a Shang-culture site at Yijiabu in Fufeng County, Baoji, Shaanxi.

entries.name: Wei River 渭水
entries.note: the Wei, the river of the Guanzhong, joining the Yellow River at Tongguan.

entries.name: Qishui River 漆水河
entries.note: a northern tributary of the Wei in central Shaanxi, flowing past Wugong and Fufeng.

entries.name: Zhouyuan 周原
entries.note: the Zhou plain north of the Wei, between Qishan and Fufeng, Shaanxi, the early seat of the Zhou.

entries.name: Binzhou 彬州
entries.note: Binzhou (formerly Bin County) on the Jing River, Xianyang, Shaanxi.

entries.name: Xunyi 旬邑
entries.note: Xunyi County on the upper Jing, Xianyang, Shaanxi, east of Binzhou.

entries.name: 诸侯 the Lords
entries.note: the rulers of the states, collectively; in this period the kings of the warring states and the lesser lords, as distinct from the Zhou king.

entries.note: to form the 合纵 (hezong) alliance, the north–south ("vertical") league of the eastern states against Qin; 从 stands for 纵.

entries.note: picked, first-rate soldiers.

entries.note: the nine bronze tripod cauldrons held to have been cast by Yu and passed from dynasty to dynasty as the emblem of legitimate rule; their removal to Qin in 256 BC marks the end of Zhou.

entries.note: the basic unit of direct administration, capitalized as an administrative unit.

entries.note: a holder of a fief granted by a king.

pages.label: 256 BC · Ivar the Boneless' commentary and analysis II

entries.name: 太后 Queen Dowager
entries.note: the mother of a reigning king.

entries.name: 后 Queen
entries.note: the principal wife of a king.

entries.name: 如夫人 secondary consort
entries.note: a consort of a king below the rank of Queen.

entries.name: 社 altar of the soil
entries.note: the altar of the god of the soil of a state or settlement.

pages.label: 256 BC · Shiji, supplement: the Eight Treatises

entries.name: 弃市 executed in the marketplace
entries.note: put to death publicly, the body exposed in the market.

entries.name: 相国 Chancellor of State
entries.note: the chief minister, addressed by his full title.

entries.name: 关内侯 Marquis within the Passes
entries.note: a lord whose land lies inside Qin's passes: a dependant of Qin.

entries.name: 社稷 altars of soil and grain
entries.note: the altars of a state's gods of soil and grain, standing for the state itself.

entries.name: 宗庙 ancestral temple
entries.note: the temple of a ruling house's ancestors.

entries.name: 帝 Emperor
entries.note: the title above king, claimed by Qin and Qi in these years.

entries.name: 布衣 commoner
entries.note: literally one in hempen clothes: a man without rank.

entries.name: 傅 Tutor
entries.note: the officer in charge of an heir's upbringing.

entries.name: 与国 allied state
entries.note: a state bound by treaty.

entries.name: 万乘 ten thousand chariots
entries.note: the measure of a great state's strength; a ruler of ten thousand chariots is a king.

entries.name: 海内 within the seas
entries.note: the whole inhabited world.

entries.name: 关 Pass
entries.note: a fortified pass.

entries.name: 令尹 Chief Minister
entries.note: the chief minister of Chu, the lingyin.

entries.name: 吏 officer
entries.note: a man in government service below the rank of official; a clerk or functionary.

entries.name: 郊 suburban sacrifice
entries.note: the sacrifice to Heaven offered by a ruler at an altar outside the city.

entries.name: 上帝 High God
entries.note: the supreme deity, Shangdi, to whom the suburban sacrifice is made.

entries.name: 八子 Bazi consort
entries.note: a rank of royal consort below the Queen; Xu Guang: the title of a secondary wife.

entries.name: 柱国 Pillar of the State
entries.note: a high office of Chu, next in rank to the Chief Minister (令尹).

entries.name: 金 jin of gold
entries.note: the unit in which sums of gold are reckoned: a yi 镒 under the Warring States and Qin, a jin 斤 under Han.

247 BC · Ivar the Boneless' commentary and analysis I

entries.name: 大夫 Grand Master
entries.note: a rank of officials below the ministers (卿).

entries.name: 丞相 Chancellor
entries.note: the head of the administration; the fuller form of the title the texts also write as 相.

entries.name: 绶 seal-ribbon
entries.note: the silk ribbon by which the seal of office was hung from the belt.

entries.name: 假相国 Acting Chancellor of State
entries.note: the office of Chancellor of State held provisionally.

entries.name: 侯 Marquis
entries.note: the holder of a marquisate, the fief named before the title.

entries.name: 舍人 household retainer
entries.note: a retainer attached to a lord's household.

entries.name: 传舍 post-house
entries.note: a lodging on the roads for travellers on official business.

entries.name: 上客 guest of the first rank
entries.note: the highest grade of a lord's retainers.

entries.name: 歃血 smear the blood
entries.note: to seal a covenant by smearing the lips with the blood of the victim.

entries.name: 守相 Acting Chancellor
entries.note: the office of Chancellor held provisionally (守); the Biography of Lian Po writes 假相国.

entries.name: 谥 posthumous title
entries.note: the title conferred on a ruler after his death, by which he is thereafter named.

entries.name: 单于 Chanyu
entries.note: the title of the ruler of the Xiongnu.

pages.label: 250 BC · Ivar the Boneless' commentary and analysis I

entries.name: 襜褴 the Danlan
entries.note: a Hu people north of Dai (Ru Chun).

pages.label: 250 BC · Ivar the Boneless' commentary and analysis I

entries.name: 东胡 the Donghu
entries.note: the Hu people east of the Xiongnu, on Yan's and Zhao's northern frontier.

pages.label: 250 BC · Ivar the Boneless' commentary and analysis I

entries.name: 林胡 the Linhu
entries.note: the Hu people of the forests on Zhao's northern frontier.

pages.label: 250 BC · Ivar the Boneless' commentary and analysis I

entries.name: 莫府 headquarters
entries.note: the office of a general in the field, under tents (幕); written 莫 for 幕.

pages.label: 250 BC · Ivar the Boneless' commentary and analysis I

entries.name: 假相 Acting Chancellor
entries.note: the office of Chancellor held provisionally (假); the Biography of Lian Po writes 假相国.

entries.name: 上卿 Senior Minister
entries.note: the highest rank of minister (卿).

entries.name: 户 household
entries.note: the household, the unit by which a fief's population and revenue were reckoned.

entries.name: 相邦 Chancellor of State
entries.note: the title as written in Warring States inscriptions; Han texts write 相国, avoiding the name of Gaozu, Liu Bang.

248 BC · Ivar the Boneless' commentary and analysis II

entries.name: 鈹 pi blade
entries.note: a straight double-edged blade mounted on a long haft, often inscribed with the year and the officials who oversaw its making.

pages.label: 249 BC · Ivar the Boneless' commentary and analysis I
248 BC · Ivar the Boneless' commentary and analysis II

entries.name: 霸 hegemon
entries.note: the lord who holds the leadership of the Lords.

entries.name: 君长 chieftain
entries.note: the head of a small or dependent people, below the rank of king.

entries.name: 衛戍病院 garrison hospital
entries.note: a military hospital of a garrison town.

entries.name: 旅 brigade
entries.note: the army unit of the period between regiment and division.

entries.name: 決死隊 death squad
entries.note: a party of volunteers for an assault from which return is not expected.

entries.name: 軍醫 army doctor
entries.note: a medical officer of the army.

entries.name: 滿鐵 the South Manchuria Railway
entries.note: the South Manchuria Railway Company (南滿洲鐵道), the Japanese railway concern in Manchuria.

entries.name: 赤十字 the Red Cross
entries.note: the Red Cross society.

entries.name: 渤海艦隊 the Bohai Fleet
entries.note: the naval squadron on the Zhili side in 1924, based at Qingdao and Qinhuangdao.

entries.name: 陸戰隊 marines
entries.note: a navy's landing force.

entries.name: 奉天軍 the Fengtian army
entries.note: the forces of the Fengtian clique; also written 奉軍.

entries.name: 副司令 deputy commander
entries.note: the second in command of an army.

entries.name: 旅長 brigade commander
entries.note: the officer commanding a brigade.

entries.name: 直隸軍 the Zhili army
entries.note: the forces of the Zhili clique; also written 直軍.

entries.name: 總司令 commander-in-chief
entries.note: the officer in supreme command.

entries.name: 内史 Clerk of the Capital
entries.note: the office governing the home territory of Qin about the capital.

pages.label: 249 BC · Qin slips in the Yuelu Academy collection

entries.name: 西工室 the Western Workshop
entries.note: a state workshop (工室) of Qin, staffed with convicts and men on labour service; the statute does not say where it stood. A Qin Western Workshop (西工) of Shu Commandery is attested on slips excavated at Zikujie, Chengdu.

pages.label: 249 BC · Qin slips in the Yuelu Academy collection

entries.name: 司寇 sikou
entries.note: the lightest grade of Qin convict labour, 'robber-guard', ranking between commoners and the lichenqie 隶臣妾 slaves; by Han law a term of two years.

pages.label: 249 BC · Qin slips in the Yuelu Academy collection

entries.name: 隐官 yinguan
entries.note: a person pardoned after a mutilating punishment and set to work out of public sight, 'the hidden'; a status ranked with the sikou.

pages.label: 249 BC · Qin slips in the Yuelu Academy collection

entries.name: 践更 serving one's geng turn
entries.note: performing in person one's turn (更) of statutory labour service for the government, as against hiring a substitute.

pages.label: 249 BC · Qin slips in the Yuelu Academy collection

entries.name: 五刑 the five punishments
entries.note: the five mutilating punishments of the ancient codes: tattooing, cutting off the nose, cutting off the feet, castration and death.

pages.label: 249 BC · Appendix: text of the Zhanguo Zonghengjia Shu

entries.name: 干将、莫邪 Ganjiang and Moye
entries.note: the two swords of legend, forged for the King of Wu by the smith Ganjiang and his wife Moye; the type of a fine blade.

pages.label: 249 BC · Appendix: text of the Zhanguo Zonghengjia Shu

entries.name: 騄耳 Lü'er
entries.note: one of the eight steeds of King Mu of Zhou; the type of a fine horse.

pages.label: 249 BC · Appendix: text of the Zhanguo Zonghengjia Shu

entries.name: 谈说之士 persuaders
entries.note: the itinerant counsellors who sold rulers plans of war and alliance.

pages.label: 249 BC · Appendix: text of the Zhanguo Zonghengjia Shu

entries.name: 仲父 Second Father
entries.note: the style a ruler gave a minister honoured as a father, after Duke Huan of Qi's for Guan Zhong (Zhengyi).

entries.name: 家僮 household slaves
entries.note: the bondsmen of a great house.

entries.name: 辩士 disputant
entries.note: a master of argument; a travelling rhetorician.

entries.name: 腐 castration
entries.note: the palace punishment, 宫刑; 腐罪, an offence punished by it.

entries.name: 给事中 palace attendant
entries.note: one attending within the palace.

entries.name: 宦者 eunuch
entries.note: a castrated servant of the palace.

entries.name: 郎 Court Gentleman
entries.note: a court attendant of the king's entourage; the office, as distinct from 士, the gentlemen as a class.

entries.name: 长史 Senior Clerk
entries.note: the chief secretary of a minister or office.

entries.name: 五帝 the Five Emperors
entries.note: the sage rulers before the Three Kings.

entries.name: 黔首 the black-headed people
entries.note: the common people, the Qin term.

entries.name: 廷尉 Commandant of Justice
entries.note: the chief judicial officer of Qin.

entries.name: 皇帝 Emperor
entries.note: the title the King of Qin took in 221 BC.

entries.name: 陛下 Your Majesty
entries.note: the address to the ruler, literally "beneath the steps".

entries.name: 后宫 harem
entries.note: the women's quarters of the palace, literally the "rear palace".

entries.name: 六国 the Six States
entries.note: Han, Zhao, Wei, Chu, Yan and Qi, the eastern states facing Qin.

entries.name: 关东 east of the Pass
entries.note: the lands east of Hangu Pass, the eastern states.

entries.name: 九夷 the Nine Yi
entries.note: the Yi peoples of Chu's lands (Suoyin); a set phrase for the southern peoples.

entries.name: 中商 Middle Shang
entries.note: the middle period of Shang archaeology, between the Erligang and Yinxu periods.

entries.name: 殷墟一期 Yinxu Phase I
entries.note: the first of the four phases of the Yinxu (Anyang) period, corresponding to the reigns of Pan Geng to Wu Ding.

entries.name: 朱开沟 Zhukaigou
entries.note: the Bronze Age culture of the Ordos named from the Zhukaigou site, Ejin Horo Banner, and the people who bore it.

entries.name: 蛇纹鬲 snake-pattern li
entries.note: the li tripod with applied snake-like strips, the type vessel of the Zhukaigou culture.

entries.name: 方 fang state
entries.note: the polities around the Shang, so named in the oracle-bone inscriptions.

entries.name: 犬方 the Quanfang
entries.note: a fang state of the west against which Wu Ding sent armies.

entries.name: 周方 the Zhoufang
entries.note: the Zhou as a fang state in the oracle-bone inscriptions.

entries.name: 甲骨卜辞 oracle-bone inscriptions
entries.note: the divination records of the Shang kings on turtle plastron and ox bone.

entries.name: 郑家坡文化 Zhengjiapo culture
entries.note: the late Shang-period culture of the Qishui valley named from the Zhengjiapo site, Wugong, Shaanxi.

entries.name: 京当型 Jingdang type
entries.note: the local type of Shang culture in the Zhouyuan region, named from the Jingdang site, Fufeng.

entries.name: 孙家类型 Sunjia type
entries.note: the cultural type of the upper Jing valley named from the Sunjia site, Binzhou.

entries.name: 先周文化 Proto-Zhou culture
entries.note: the archaeological culture of the Zhou before the conquest of Shang.

entries.name: 西土 the western lands
entries.note: the lands west of the Shang, as the oracle-bone inscriptions call them.

entries.name: 方方 the Fang
entries.note: the fang state named Fang 方 in the oracle-bone inscriptions, a people of the north-west under Wu Ding.
